sections.heading: A NEW ELECTRIC GIRL SHORT STORY, PROMISED AGAIN
sections.content:
Q: Please publish an Electric Girl short story on the website, sensei, please.

A: I'll probably write one next month.

sections.heading: WILL EVERY SERIES ACTUALLY GET FINISHED?
sections.content:
Q: Six Guns, Six People, Six Days, The Lizard King, Mugen Loop Game, Adachi and Shimamura, The Fluffy Girl Falls from the Sky, N743327, LZEEHLN, God's Trash Can, Best Friend Robot Chocolate… Iruma-sensei has so many ongoing series — will you actually see all of them through to a proper ending? If possible, I'd love for Chocolate and God's Trash Can to get bunko editions soon.

A: Honestly, I feel like even if I wrote sequels, they'd probably fail to sell, so they might just not happen. That said, sales aren't actually bad enough to rule out a sequel entirely — it's stuck in this really awkward, ambiguous middle ground. In my struggle to escape that awkward spot, I ended up just... writing more series instead. Sorry for making everyone wait so long. I might not be able to perfectly meet everyone's expectations, but I'll do what I can. Also, both of those two will get bunko editions before the year is out.

sections.heading: HOW MANY SERIES AT ONCE?
sections.content:
Q: So how many series is sensei actually writing at the same time right now?

A: The person who asked the question above already listed them all for me.

sections.heading: THE ALUMINUM-ALLOY CASE HABIT
sections.content:
Q: Aluminum-alloy briefcases show up in your work pretty often — is there a particular reason for that?

A: Maybe because I actually use one myself? By the way, I originally misspelled it as "jeruminium case" the first time! So embarrassing!

sections.heading: A FAVORITE VIOLINIST
sections.content:
Q: What kind of music do you usually listen to? Spitz or BUMP OF CHICKEN, I'd guess? By the way, what I usually listen to is "New World" (Note: the theme song for Iruma Hitoma's fifth-anniversary project New World, with lyrics by Iruma, composed and arranged by Satoru Kousaki, performed by Marina Kawano).

A: Thank you, that makes me happy! What I usually listen to is Taro Hakase.[ref:taro-hakase-jonetsu]

sections.heading: WHAT TO DO WHEN INSPIRATION RUNS DRY
sections.content:
Q: Lately I feel like my inspiration for writing novels has dried up, and it's really troubling me… What does Iruma-sensei do when that happens? Have you ever hit a slump? Also, I love you the most. Please keep at it!

A: I basically never run dry, though that has nothing to do with whether what I write actually turns out good. As for a slump — the moment I remember that I need to earn a living through this work, I can't really afford to say something that defeatist. I'll do my best, thank you.

sections.heading: ADASHIMA OR DACHIMURA?
sections.content:
Q: The shortened nickname for Adachi and Shimamura seems to have settled on "Adashima," but personally, since it rolls off the tongue better, I'm on team "Dachimura" (someone else's suggestion). Is it too late to overturn the established nickname?

A: Everyone can just call it whatever they personally like. Though, I had no idea there was already a settled nickname for it.

sections.heading: THE NAKED IDIOT'S CINEMATIC LINEAGE
sections.content:
Q: Does the title of The Naked Idiot Comes Running come from the old film The Idiot Comes on a Tank?[ref:baka-tank-movie]

A: Tracing it all the way back, yes, that's exactly where it comes from. Though I actually learned this particular sentence pattern from the anime Gunparade March (Note: Episode 25 of Gunparade March is titled "The Idiot Comes Back in Powered Armor").

sections.heading: GETTING RID OF THE "VIRGIN" CURSE
sections.content:
Q: To get rid of the cursed equipment known as "virginity," it seems you need to raise your affection level enough for a girlfriend to join your party — where and how should I go about doing that?

A: If your affection level isn't high enough, she's not going to join your party.

sections.heading: A LOST STORY, STILL LOST
sections.content:
Q: I want to read Just About Invincible, Mostly a Kid (Note: a novel depicting the childhoods of characters like Kisogawa, once serialized on a now-defunct Kadokawa web platform, and now impossible to find)! Is it really gone for good? Please show us your power, sensei!

A: I'll do my best to get it published as a book within the year… I'll try hard (Note: as of this translation, it still has never been published).

sections.heading: A MESSAGE FROM CHINA
sections.content:
Q: Hello, Iruma-sensei! I'm a reader from China. Because I love your work so much, I've recently started learning Japanese, but I still haven't even memorized the kana properly. I really love The Lizard King series and want to see where the story goes next — but why has it been so long without a new volume? (Note: This question was originally submitted in Chinese. Due to differences in character encoding, several Simplified Chinese-only characters were lost when it was reproduced on Iruma no Ma. The garbled original reads roughly: "Hello Ir- sensei! I'm a read- from China. Because I lo- your work so much, I'm learn- Japan-, but I haven't memori- the kana yet. I really like the Liz-'s King series, want to see the future develop-, but why so l- without a new bo-?")

A: I'll do my best to get the sequel out.

sections.heading: HOW TO WRITE LIKE IRUMA-SENSEI
sections.content:
Q: Iruma-sensei's work is incredibly fun. What does it take to become as amazing a writer as you? I'm a foreigner, so my Japanese might be a bit off — please forgive me. _(:з」∠)_

A: Setting aside modest talk about whether I'm actually "amazing" or not — I think you probably need to observe your surroundings carefully. Observation is the foundation of everything.

sections.heading: A FAVORITE ICE CREAM
sections.content:
Q: What kind of ice cream does Iruma-sensei like? I'm personally team soft-serve cone.

A: I'm not sure if it technically counts as ice cream, but Yogorino is delicious.[ref:yogorino]

sections.heading: NOVEL-WRITING ISN'T LANGUAGE CLASS
sections.content:
Q: I write novels purely as a hobby, but I feel like I can't quite convey what I want to express through my writing. Was Iruma-sensei good at Japanese class in school? If I want to write novels, should I study Japanese language more?

A: I don't think novels and Japanese class are exactly friends, or in a teacher-student relationship with each other. What matters is racking up sheer volume. If you do that, your work will naturally become more refined. Just look at my own writing!

sections.heading: A YEAR-ROUND YUKATA HABIT
sections.content:
Q: I have a question I want to ask right away — sensei wears a kimono in daily life, but do you switch to a jinbei or yukata in summer? I also love kimono, and I've worn one in my daily life since high school, but summer is just too hot, so I lean toward a simpler jinbei or yukata. What does sensei wear in summer?

A: I wear a yukata year-round. Even in winter, I only wear a single yukata. This is basically a sickness.

sections.heading: WHEN DID THE YUKATA HABIT START?
sections.content:
Q: Does Iruma-sensei really wear a yukata no matter the season? When did you become a "yukata person"? (lol)

A: Probably right after I graduated from university. Picking clothes this way is easy, so it's pretty great.

sections.heading: MISSING OUT ON THE DENGEKI AUTUMN SIGNING
sections.content:
Q: I couldn't get a ticket to the Dengeki Autumn signing event… (crying hard) Could Iruma-sensei hold another signing event, please…?

A: Will they even invite me this year? I have no idea. I'll go ask my editor right now whether they can get me on the list for a signing. Please, invite me.

sections.heading: DESIGNING DISTINCTIVE CHARACTERS
sections.content:
Q: I'm a high-school fan of Kisogawa. His look — a dark navy suit paired with a pointed hat — is really stylish. How do you go about designing the appearance of characters like this? Iruma Hitoma's characters are always so easy to tell apart, and I'm really curious how that works.

A: I have absolutely no idea what a "normal" outfit even looks like, so my characters' appearances naturally end up deviating from the norm.

sections.heading: A POEM WRITTEN BY ADACHI?
sections.content:
Q: I'd love to read a girlish poem written by Adachi. Does Iruma-sensei ever want to read "Adachi's poetry"?

A: Since I'd be the one actually writing it, no, I don't.

sections.heading: WHY A CHICKEN?
sections.content:
Q: I finished reading My Small-Scale Suicide. It's a pretty clichéd reaction, but I thought, "whoa, that ending was really something..." — genuinely a lot of fun. By the way, why did you choose a chicken design for Leghorn's appearance? Is there some deeper meaning behind it?

A: I once thought about a story involving traveling with a rooster gentleman, so I just reused that idea. In other words, there's no deeper meaning at all.

sections.heading: VOLUME 3 ISN'T THE END
sections.content:
Q: Volume 3 of Adachi and Shimamura isn't the final one, right? My friends keep saying "every series ends eventually lol," and it's making me worried. Please tell me.

A: There'll be a fourth volume. I just can't say when.

sections.heading: A SUGOI JAPAN NOMINATION
sections.content:
Q: You've been nominated for the SUGOI JAPAN light novel award! How do you feel about it?[ref:sugoi-japan] (Note: Iruma's The Lying Boy and the Broken Girl was among the 50 works nominated in the first SUGOI JAPAN Award's Light Novel category.)

A: SUGOI! ("Amazing!")

sections.heading: AFTER, OR SPIRAL
sections.content:
Q: I heard you're considering writing a book about Akkyun and Ma-chan's daughter — will Akkyun and Ma-chan themselves make a cameo in it? If possible, I'd love another full book about Akkyun and Ma-chan themselves. I love them both the most. And Iruma-sensei too, the most. Sorry, I added that last part after the fact.

A: Rather than a "cameo," I'd say the two of them would naturally appear anyway, simply by being the parents. Let's just treat this new book as a continuation of Akkyun and Ma-chan's story. Maybe I'll slap "After" or "Spiral" onto the title or something.

sections.heading: A LOOSE APPROACH TO KIMONO
sections.content:
Q: When I went to your signing event, you were wearing a kimono — do you just really like kimono? If you have any tips for wearing one, please share them.

A: I do like kimono, but I wear mine pretty carelessly, because I don't want to be too uptight about it. That's basically my excuse for wanting to keep it low-effort.

sections.heading: BUNKO EDITIONS ON THE WAY
sections.content:
Q: Are God's Trash Can and Best Friend Robot, both serialized in Dengeki Bunko MAGAZINE, scheduled for bunko releases? Please let us know if possible!

A: God's Trash Can is scheduled for a February release, and Best Friend Robot is also scheduled to come out soon. Thanks for your patience.

sections.heading: WHEN'S THE NEXT VOLUME OF EACH?
sections.content:
Q: When will new volumes of Six Guns, Six People, Six Days and the Hanasaki Tarou series come out?

A: I'll do my best to get them out this year… I think 666 will probably make it out.

sections.heading: BREAD OR RICE FOR BREAKFAST?
sections.content:
Q: Do you eat breakfast every day? Also, are you team bread or team rice?

A: I lean toward bread, I think. I generally eat all three meals properly. After all, I live at my parents' house.

sections.heading: ELLIO'S UNDISCLOSED BIRTHDAY
sections.content:
Q: I love Electric Girl and Adolescent Boy and read the whole thing. I recall the story mentioning the birthdays of Jojo's aunt, Makoto, and Ryuushi-kun, but the heroine Ellio's birthday never actually came up. Has Ellio's birthday been decided? I'm really curious! Please let me know if you've already worked it out.

A: How about setting it as the release date of E.T.?[ref:et-birthday]

sections.heading: WHY NOT USE TWITTER?
sections.content:
Q: Does Iruma-sensei use Twitter?

A: If I had spare time to write posts there, it'd be more productive to spend it writing novels instead. Besides, I don't think I really have anything worth posting. Even if I did start using Twitter, I'd probably just end up constantly reporting things like "had ___ for lunch, it was good. Had ___ for dinner, it was good."

sections.heading: WHAT COUNTS AS A LIE?
sections.content:
Q: So, sensei, how would you define a lie? I'm someone who's pretty good at lying myself.

A: A lie is anything you can't accept. If you can accept it, then no matter how twisted it's become, it counts as truth. Acceptance matters more than anything else… et cetera.

sections.heading: HOW TO GET ALONG LIKE MAKOTO AND ELLIO
sections.content:
Q: How can I become as close with someone as Makoto and Ellio are?

A: Understand what kind of self the other person hopes you'll be, listen carefully to what they have to say, and find the right person.

sections.heading: A LOCAL REFERENCE, REDACTED PAST RECOGNITION
sections.content:
Q: Please keep using more local references going forward — it'd make me really happy. That shop that closed down, hmm~ was it ○○○-tei, or Ko○○○?

A: Probably neither, honestly. Also, you've censored it so heavily that I can't even tell what you're asking about.

sections.heading: DOES HE LIKE HIS OWN OLDER WORK?
sections.content:
Q: In From the Bottom of Europa, you wrote that you're not particularly fond of your older work — is that connected to why Akkyun and Ma-chan rarely appear in your other stories? I'd appreciate it if you could answer, if you get the chance. Thank you.

A: I feel like they've actually shown up plenty of times — Electric Girl, The Lizard King, 666... though now that I think about it, aside from Six Guns, Six People, Six Days, those have all just been side-story cameos, haven't they? To avoid any misunderstanding, I should clarify up front — the book you're referring to is fictional. Generally speaking, I never project myself into my own work at all. So it's not really a matter of liking or disliking it. It's just that some characters are difficult for me to write, and those two happen to fall into that category.

sections.heading: A SHARED FAVORITE YURI PAIRING
sections.content:
Q: I also love Sakurako and Himawari from Yuru○○○! Yay! It's exciting and a little embarrassing at once (/ω＼).

A: I've also been watching Oomuro-ke — it's a lot of fun. Alright, maybe I should write a Hino family or Nagafuji family spin-off too… ah, though I mean as a bonus feature tacked onto the main series.

sections.heading: A GUNDAM PREFERENCE, AND A BATHROOM QUESTION
sections.content:
Q: I'm anxious about the future — if I had to pilot a mobile suit, should I go with Asshimar or Force? Also, when you use toilet paper, are you team double-ply, or team finger?

A: I like Major Bran,[ref:gundam-bran] so I'm team Asshimar. Also, what on earth does "team finger" even mean?

sections.heading: GO WRITE YOUR OWN NOVEL
sections.content:
Q: Iruma-tan, the free meal was so delicious! One: why hasn't the bunko edition of The Isolated come out yet? Two: please hurry up and put out new volumes of your other series. Three: sorry for being so rude — but I don't want to trouble other people, so maybe I just shouldn't work at all. Four: please scold me and tell me, "don't do that, go write your own novel instead."

A: Go write your own novel.

sections.heading: A GIFU MASCOT REQUEST
sections.content:
Q: Sensei's from Gifu, right? Speaking of Gifu, I think of Sarubobo. Is Sarubobo basically a household god (?) where you're from?[ref:sarubobo] (Note: Sarubobo is a longstanding good-luck charm doll from the Hida region in northern Gifu Prefecture.) My friend used to have a plush Sarubobo, and it was really cute. I'd love one too — could you send me one? I'll treat you to some anmitsu as thanks.

A: There really is a mountain of Sarubobo merchandise over in Hida, but pretty much none of it exists on my end of the prefecture. So I can't get my hands on one — sorry about that.

sections.heading: WRITING WHAT YOU LOVE VS. LOVING WHAT YOU WRITE
sections.content:
Q: I love yuri stories the most, and I love your Adachi and Shimamura too. But whenever I try writing a yuri story myself, I can never quite get it to go the way I want, and I can't produce anything I'm satisfied with. Is what you enjoy reading really just different from what you enjoy writing?

A: That's obviously going to be different. I love Dragon Ball, but I'm terrible at writing combat-focused fiction.

sections.heading: THE LIZARD KING'S STALLED FIFTH VOLUME
sections.content:
Q: Does The Lizard King really end at Volume 5? Also, when does Volume 3 of Six Guns, Six People, Six Days come out?

A: Within the year… is what I'd like to say, but there are some grown-up circumstances on the Lizard King side of things…

sections.heading: ANY WORD ON A NEW LIZARD KING VOLUME?
sections.content: Q: When will a new volume of The Lizard King be released?

sections.heading: READING BETWEEN THE LINES
sections.content: Q: Grown-up circumstances… I think he's the type of person who rises to the occasion when it really counts. But wait, who am I even talking about? (Note: it's commonly speculated that The Lizard King's inability to get a sequel out is related to illustrator Buriki's circumstances.)

sections.heading: A QUIET NEW YEAR'S
sections.content:
Q: Happy New Year. How did sensei spend New Year's Eve and New Year's Day? Also, did you go do a New Year's shrine visit?

A: Happy New Year to you too. On New Year's Day, I played hanafuda with my family. Going out for a shrine visit felt like too much trouble, so I skipped it.

references.title: Taro Hakase and Jounetsu Tairiku
references.note: A repeat reference to violinist Taro Hakase (previously named as a favorite performer in Round 7). He is well known in Japan for composing the theme music for the long-running TV documentary series Jounetsu Tairiku ("Passion Continent").

references.title: The Idiot Comes on a Tank
references.note: Baka ga Tank de Yattekuru ("The Idiot Comes on a Tank") is a 1964 Japanese comedy film directed by Yoji Yamada, the third entry in the "Baka" ("Idiot") film series starring comedian Hana Hajime. Its title structure — "[type of fool] comes via [vehicle/method]" — was later riffed on by the 2001 mecha anime Gunparade March in an episode titled "The Idiot Comes Back in Powered Armor," which is where Iruma says he actually picked up the pattern, before tracing it back to its original source.

references.title: Yogorino
references.note: Yogorino is a real Italian yogurt-gelato brand, marketed as a low-fat, low-calorie treat and popular in Italy; it also has a licensed presence in Japan and other parts of Asia.

references.title: The SUGOI JAPAN Award
references.note: The SUGOI JAPAN Award was a contest first held in 2015, presented by the Yomiuri Shimbun newspaper, recognizing outstanding works across manga, anime, light novels, and general entertainment fiction via public and expert nomination and voting.

references.title: E.T. as a Birthday Reference
references.note: Iruma jokingly suggests basing Ellio's birthday on the release date of Steven Spielberg's E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial — a fitting joke given Ellio's own alien-adjacent backstory in Electric Girl and Adolescent Boy, and a callback to an earlier Q&A where Iruma mentioned an unfinished web short story titled "E.T." featuring Elliott and Jojo's daughter.

references.title: Asshimar, Major Bran, and the Gundam Franchise
references.note: The Asshimar is a transformable mobile armor from Mobile Suit Zeta Gundam. Major Bran Bland is a recurring supporting officer across multiple entries in the original Universal Century Gundam timeline. Iruma's answer suggests a personal fondness for that corner of the franchise, though the specific connection he's drawing between the character and the mobile suit isn't made fully explicit in his answer.

references.title: Sarubobo
references.note: Sarubobo ("monkey baby" in the local Hida dialect) is a traditional faceless doll handcrafted in the Hida region of northern Gifu Prefecture, historically given as a charm for safe childbirth, good relationships, and children's health, and now a widely sold regional souvenir.
